bounded_statement: The selected result — a paired t-test on 36 flush-event pairs reporting mean gain 0.300 mg/L (SD 0.100 mg/L), t(35) = 18.000, p < 0.0001 — is produced by entering all 36 rows of data/input.csv into scipy.stats.ttest_rel, a procedure that treats each pre/post pair as an independent observation. The data description names hydrant_id as the independent-unit column and states each of the 12 hydrants contributes three rows, so each independent unit enters the row-independent test three times. The degrees of freedom (35 instead of 11) and the p-value/precision are therefore overstated and not supported as reported; the mean gain of 0.300 mg/L itself, and the qualitative direction of the effect (a hydrant-level reanalysis on 12 hydrant-mean gains still gives t(11) ≈ 10.2), are not affected.

counterevidence_considered.description: The report is transparent that it analysed 36 event-level pairs rather than concealing the unit of analysis, and the pre/post pairing within each row is itself legitimate; the point estimate of the mean gain (0.300 mg/L) is identical whether computed over 36 rows or 12 hydrant means, so the effect-size claim is not distorted by the repeated entry.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: mean gain 0.300 mg/L at both row level and hydrant level

counterevidence_considered.description: All 36 row-level gains are positive (from +0.18 for HYD-01 up to +0.42 for HYD-12), and a correct hydrant-level reanalysis on the 12 hydrant-mean gains (mean 0.300, SD ≈ 0.102) gives t(11) ≈ 10.2, still rejecting the no-change null far below the 5 percent level. The qualitative conclusion in the Reading section therefore survives correct handling of the independent unit; what is unsupported is the reported t(35), SD-based precision, and p-value magnitude.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: hydrant-level reanalysis: n = 12, mean gain 0.300 mg/L, SD ≈ 0.102 mg/L, t(11) ≈ 10.2, p ≈ 1e-6

Hand recomputation reproduces it exactly from the row-level data (mean gain 0.300, SD 0.100, t = 0.300/(0.100/sqrt(36)) = 18.0), confirming all 36 rows were entered as independent pairs.

The two readings attached to a flush event form a natural pair, so the
post-minus-pre gain was analysed with a two-sided paired t-test
(`scipy.stats.ttest_rel`) over the 36 event-level pairs.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to defeat the finding three ways. (1) I searched workflow/analysis.py for any grouping, deduplication, or aggregation by hydrant_id that would reduce the data to one entry per independent unit; there is none — the hydrant_id column is never read anywhere in the script. (2) I considered whether the flush event, rather than the hydrant, could legitimately be treated as the independent unit; the data description explicitly names hydrant_id as the independent-unit column and states each hydrant contributes three repeated rows, so event-level independence is not authorized by the supplied description. (3) I recomputed the statistics by hand: the 36 row-level gains have mean 0.300 and SD 0.100, reproducing the reported t(35) = 18.000 exactly, which confirms the test was run over all 36 rows; collapsing to 12 hydrant-mean gains yields t(11) ≈ 10.2 with SD ≈ 0.102, showing the reported df = 35 and t = 18.000 depend specifically on entering each hydrant three times. None of these attempts overturned the finding; the strongest mitigating fact (the hydrant-level test remains significant) affects severity, not whether the issue class is present.

root_cause: workflow/analysis.py's read_pairs iterates csv.DictReader over every row and appends the pre- and post-reline readings without ever reading or grouping by the hydrant_id column; main then sets n = len(before) = 36, runs stats.ttest_rel(after, before) over all rows, and reports df = n - 1 = 35. The three repeated visits per hydrant are never aggregated or modelled, so the row-independent paired t-test receives each of the 12 independent units (hydrants) three times.
